facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s with a 10-year history of Crohn disease
intermittent bowel obstructions leading to total proctocolectomy and ileostomy
Five weeks after his surgery, he developed a painful, erosive lesion around his stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions were present
Repeated cultures were negative
Revealed epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay showed high level of IgG autoantibodies
Against desmoglein 1: 40 IU/mL (normal value: 20 U/mL)
Against desmoglein 3: 90 IU/mL (normal value: 20 U/mL)
A painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showing suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis (original magnification ×100)

concepts.why: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and 3, and intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis, are characteristic of Pemphigus
The development of a painful, erosive lesion around the stoma site is a known complication of stoma formation
The patient's history of Crohn disease and the presence of autoantibodies suggest an autoimmune component to the enteropathy
The development of a complication at the ileostomy site is a known risk of the procedure

The presence of a painful, erosive lesion at the stoma site, with histopathological findings of epidermal erosion and suprabasal epidermal splitting, is consistent with peristomal pyoderma gangrenosum
It explains the histopathological finding of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis.
